children.game_version: The 'Snake King' game: children wear paper snake crowns and must tell a story using only their hands while moving as slowly as possible.

avoid: Overextending the neck while wearing heavy headgear
seniors.counts: Slow 1-2-3-4 counts following the Mallika metre.
seniors.seated_version: The dance is highly suitable for a seated version as it emphasizes hand gestures and an erect upper body.
seniors.standing_version: Perform while standing near a support; the minimal footwork makes it accessible for those with limited mobility.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Maintain the original slow tempo; reduce the range of arm extensions if shoulder mobility is limited.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Extensive use of gestures to explain the meanings of the songs
movement_profile.footwork: Very little dance element; primarily standing
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Solo performer standing in a central position
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Minimal movement; focus is on the upper body and facial expression
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: None described; focus is on the standing level

signature_moves.description: The performer stands straight, focusing all energy into the hand gestures and facial expressions.
signature_moves.name: Erect Narrative Stance

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid fast or jerky movements which contradict the slow tempo and spiritual nature of the form.

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Steady, slow rhythmic cycles dictated by the poetic verse
music_profile.sound_description: A slow-paced vocal recitation of Sanskrit-influenced poetry, where the rhythm is governed by the Mallika metre, creating a steady and meditative atmosphere.
music_profile.vocal_style: Poetic recitation and singing of spiritual stories

basic_steps: Begin hand gestures (mudras) to mirror the sung verse
Maintain minimal lower body movement while pivoting to face the audience
teaching.level_notes: Requires high proficiency in mudras (hand gestures) and knowledge of Sanskrit-based poetry.
teaching.rhythm: Slow, based on the Mallika Sanskrit metre
